title: 억양: 밥 먹어요? / 밥 먹어요.
objective: Read a short -요 sentence as a question by raising your voice, or as a statement by letting it fall.
summary: The same Korean sentence can be a question or a statement; only the tone at the end changes.

task.title: Read, mark, and answer
task.line: Read each sentence aloud. Then mark the tone, add the right punctuation, or write the sentence.

words.exampleMeaning: Are you eating? — Yes, I am.
Are you going to school? — Yes, I am.

words.meaning: to like; to be good (here: to like)
words.exampleMeaning: Do you like this song? — Yes, I do.
Do you have any water? — Yes, here it is.

letters.sound: Question: raise your voice on the last syllable 요.
letters.as: Like English "Coffee?" when you offer it.

letters.sound: Statement: let your voice drop gently on 요.
letters.as: Like English "I'm eating." at the end of a sentence.

letters.sound: Answers start with 네 or 아니요. Say them calmly, with a falling tone.

exercises: Rising (↗) or falling (↘)? Read each sentence aloud and mark the end: ① 커피 마셔요? ② 네, 마셔요. ③ 지금 와요?
Add ? or . at the end: ① You ask a friend: 지금 자요__ ② Your friend answers: 아니요, 공부해요__ ③ You tell someone where you are going: 시장에 가요__
Change each statement into a question and read it with a rising end: ① 친구가 와요. ② 비가 와요.
Answer with the word given in brackets. Let your voice fall at the end: ① 우유 사요? (네) ② 영화 봐요? (네) ③ 한국어 어려워요? (아니요, 쉬워요)
Minsu says 숙제해요. Is he asking or telling? ① His voice goes up at the end (↗). ② His voice goes down at the end (↘).
answers: ① 지금 자요? ② 아니요, 공부해요. ③ 시장에 가요.
① 친구가 와요? ② 비가 와요?
① 네, 우유 사요. (네, 사요.) ② 네, 영화 봐요. (네, 봐요.) ③ 아니요, 쉬워요.
① Asking: "Are you doing homework?" ② Telling: "I'm doing homework."
